chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ismail, from Al-Fadl ibn Shazan, all from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid, from Ubaydullah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
Regarding the Words of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: 'Have you not seen those to whom it was said: Withhold your hands?' He said: 'It means: Restrain your tongues.'
ai.seo_question: What does the Quranic command 'Withhold your hands' mean according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) offers a nuanced exegetical insight into Surah An-Nisa 4:77, interpreting the command to 'withhold your hands' not merely as physical restraint but as a directive to guard the tongue from speech. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on *hilm* (forbearance) and the ethical discipline of speech as a primary form of jihad al-nafs, linking physical stillness to verbal restraint. It underscores the practical implication that in times of tribulation, preserving one's tongue is as critical as preserving one's body.
